'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Afghanistan conflict (1978–present)|Afghanistan conflict]]
**Four women, including an activist, are killed by gunmen in the city of [[Mazar-i-Sharif]], [[Balkh Province]]. Two suspects are arrested. [https://www.france24.com/en/asia-pacific/20211106-four-women-slain-in-afghanistan-after-phone-call-to-join-evacuation-flight (France 24)]
*[[Tigray War]]
**A day after urging its citizens to leave [[Ethiopia]], the [[U.S. government]] orders its embassy in [[Addis Ababa]] to evacuate non-emergency personnel due to [[armed conflict]], [[civil unrest]] and potential supply shortages. [https://www.jpost.com/breaking-news/us-orders-government-employees-in-ethiopia-to-leave-684206 (''The Jerusalem Post'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*Eleven people are killed and six others are injured in a fire at the [[intensive care unit]] of a hospital in [[Ahmednagar]], [[India]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/11/6/several-killed-fire-indian-hospital-covid-ward (Al Jazeera)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Greece]]
****[[Greece]] imposes new restrictions that require [[COVID-19 vaccination in Greece|unvaccinated]] people to show a negative [[rapid test|rapid]] or [[Polymerase chain reaction|PCR]] test in order to enter retail stores, banks, public offices, mixed entertainment venues and hairdressers and also require unvaccinated children to show a negative self-test in order to enter any establishments that cater to a mixed clientele. [https://www.ekathimerini.com/news/1171270/restrictions-on-unvaccinated-come-into-effect/ (''Ekathimerini'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
****[[Russia]] reports a record 41,335 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 8,755,930. [https://www.newsweek.com/russia-covid-vaccine-sputnik-lockdown-death-toll-pandemic-1646677 (Newsweek)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Ukraine]]
****[[Ukraine]] reports a record 793 [[COVID-19 pandemic deaths|deaths]] from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 71,635. [https://apnews.com/article/coronavirus-pandemic-europe-health-ukraine-kyiv-07dffd744202f6072d63099fa736b078 (AP)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Australia]]
****The number of people over the age of 16 years old who have been vaccinated against [[COVID-19]] in [[Australia]] surpasses 80%, which is the major milestone set by the [[Australian Government|federal government]] for its vaccination program. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2021-11-06/pm-hails-80pc-vaccine-milestone/100600132 (ABC News Australia)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand]]
****[[New Zealand]] reports a record for the second consecutive day of 206 new cases of COVID-19, which is the first time that the country has reported more than 200 cases since the beginning of the [[pandemic]]. [https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/covid-19-delta-outbreak-206-new-cases-200-in-auckland-four-in-waikato-two-in-far-north/NHQIB6PDIFDSQZJ3CWEDPMTOPQ/ (''New Zealand Herald'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Costa Rica]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Costa Rica]]
***[[Costa Rica]] issues a new mandate that would require children over the age of five years old to be vaccinated against COVID-19, making it one of the first countries to introduce such a mandate as part of its basic vaccination campaign. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-costa-rica-vaccine/costa-rica-issues-covid-19-vaccine-requirement-for-children-idUSKBN2HR0HZ (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia]]
***[[Malaysia]] reports its first two cases of the [[SARS-CoV-2 Delta variant|Delta subvariant]] AY.4.2 from two Malaysian students who returned from the [[United Kingdom]] on October 2 and tested positive on October 7. [https://www.nst.com.my/news/nation/2021/11/743067/malaysia-confirms-first-two-cases-covid-19-delta-plus-variant (''New Straits Times'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*A man [[mass stabbing|stabs passengers]] on an [[Intercity Express|express train]] between the cities of [[Regensburg]] and [[Nuremberg]] in [[Bavaria]], [[Germany]], injuring three people. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/three-injured-knife-attack-german-train-2021-11-06/ (Reuters)]
